memory_update.text: Use Micron as the US-listed reference anchor for HBM/DRAM capacity tightness, but avoid letting it crowd out supplier-level candidates in later layers.
FormFactor is a high-priority underfollowed HBM test candidate because its product page explicitly references HBM known-good-die/stack probe-card support.
Camtek is a high-priority inspection/metrology candidate because it has disclosed recent HBM and OSAT order flow, including a June 2026 $105M-plus order announcement.
Amkor is a direct advanced-packaging/test capacity candidate and onshoring beneficiary, but later layers must verify customer commitments, utilization, timing, and margin impact.

Layer 1B still needs a separate search pass for smaller speculative suppliers in thermal interface materials, underfill, ABF substrates, test handlers/contactors, enterprise SSD controllers, and refurbished/circular enterprise memory channels.
CAMT should be tracked as a direct HBM/heterogeneous-integration inspection-metrology underfollowed candidate; explicit tier-1 HBM order evidence exists.
COHU should be tracked as a lower-attention HBM inspection/metrology candidate through its Neon platform selection by a leading US memory/data-storage customer.
AEHR is not yet a confirmed HBM supplier but belongs in speculative shadow tracking for high-bandwidth flash, memory wafer-level burn-in, and AI processor burn-in spillovers.

Need a follow-up pass on US-listed advanced-packaging materials and substrate-adjacent suppliers: underfill, thermal-interface materials, electroplating/chemicals, ABF-related inputs, and consumables are not fully covered in this 4-candidate limit.
MU should remain a reference anchor for the HBM/DRAM node, but not the main underfollowed discovery target because attention and market-cap are high.
FORM is a high-relevance probe-card candidate for HBM yield and known-good-die testing; future layers should quantify HBM contribution to DRAM probe-card revenue.
COHU is a lower-attention HBM inspection/test-handler candidate with explicit but still small HBM revenue guidance; survival depends on evidence that HBM revenue scales materially.
ONTO is a process-control and advanced-packaging metrology candidate; include despite large-cap status because exposure to HBM/2.5D yield gates is unusually direct.

Still need a later pass on US-listed substrate, thermal-interface-material, underfill, refurbished-enterprise-hardware, distributor, and secondary-memory-channel names; this pass mainly captured probe, test, metrology, and direct-memory anchors.
COHU is a high-relevance underfollowed HBM inspection/metrology candidate with explicit HBM customer orders and small but disclosed HBM revenue.

FORM is a strong HBM probe-card candidate; direct HBM evidence is strong, but market cap is slightly above the preferred $300M-$10B hunting range, so it should be tracked as an unusually pure large-cap exposure.

PENG is a second-order memory-spillover candidate tied to enterprise AI inference, Integrated Memory, and CXL-based MemoryAI; evidence is promising but needs validation that growth is structural rather than pricing-cycle driven.

Still need a follow-up pass for US-listed substrate, underfill, thermal-interface, ABF-material, and advanced-packaging consumables suppliers; current pass is stronger in test/probe and memory-infrastructure spillovers.

node: HBM, DRAM wafers, advanced packaging, substrates, test/inspection, and enterprise memory/storage spillovers
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B universe expansion found one direct reference memory maker and three US-listed underfollowed or less-obvious suppliers tied to HBM/AI packaging capacity: Micron as the obvious HBM/DRAM anchor; FormFactor in wafer probe/probe cards for HBM known-good-die/stack testing; Camtek in inspection/metrology with explicit HBM and advanced-packaging orders; and Amkor in outsourced advanced packaging/test capacity for AI/HPC. The most Serenity-relevant underfollowed lanes are test/probe and inspection/metrology because they sit one step behind HBM and GPU demand and can become yield/capacity chokepoints without being the headline memory producer. Layer 1B expansion found one obvious US-listed HBM/memory anchor and three more underfollowed or shadow suppliers tied to HBM inspection, metrology, test/burn-in, or memory-capacity spillovers. The cleanest underfollowed evidence in this pass is CAMT and COHU, both with explicit HBM inspection/metrology exposure. AEHR is included as a speculative shadow candidate because its public materials point to AI processor burn-in and high-bandwidth flash / future DRAM wafer-level burn-in opportunities, but direct HBM revenue evidence still needs verification. Layer 1B expands the US-listed universe for the HBM/DRAM/advanced-packaging chokepoint with one obvious memory reference anchor and three less-obvious equipment or process-control beneficiaries. The underfollowed lane is strongest where HBM creates testing, probe-card, inspection, metrology, and yield-management bottlenecks rather than simple semiconductor-cycle exposure. This is research
